questions.question: What characterizes the 'parallel perform' phase of knowledge transfer?
options: A) The instructor performs all tasks while the trainee observes
B) The trainee performs 100% of the tasks while the instructor observes
C) The trainee performs 50% of tasks with instructor assistance
D) The trainee works independently without any supervision
questions.answer: B) The trainee performs 100% of the tasks while the instructor observes
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Parallel perform means you are doing it 100 percent, he is observing you because he has to observe you are now actually solving a problem.'

questions.question: When does the 'transfer of service responsibility' typically occur in the transition process?
options: A) After guided perform
B) After assisted perform
C) After parallel perform
D) At the very beginning of the transition
questions.answer: C) After parallel perform
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'transfer of service responsibility comes in after only after parallel perform.'

questions.question: What significant risk is highlighted regarding the experts who provide training during the transition phase?
options: A) They might demand higher salaries
B) They might leave the company after the transition, making follow-up questions difficult
C) They might intentionally provide incorrect information
D) They might refuse to use remote knowledge transfer tools
questions.answer: B) They might leave the company after the transition, making follow-up questions difficult
questions.explanation: The lecture warns, 'you have to be aware of the people who are training giving you the training they are the people who are going to lose their job... after that if you have any questions etcetera, etcetera they are not there.'

questions.question: What does the acronym GDC stand for in the context of RKT infrastructure?
options: A) Global Data Center
B) General Development Code
C) Global Delivery Center
D) Government Digital Cloud
questions.answer: C) Global Delivery Center
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'GDC means stands for Global Delivery Center that is what the centers we call in India, located in India the global delivery centers.'

questions.question: Which of the following is a key deliverable during the 'application specific planning' phase?
options: A) Final service level agreements
B) Disaster recovery plan
C) Training plan
D) Steady state delivery organization
questions.answer: C) Training plan
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Training plan of course, there is training plan' under application specific planning deliverables.

questions.question: Why is it important to have a risk plan and mitigation strategies during transition planning?
options: A) To ensure all employees are satisfied
B) To prevent any project delays
C) To address potential issues like connectivity, server problems, or manpower loss
D) To reduce the overall cost of the project
questions.answer: C) To address potential issues like connectivity, server problems, or manpower loss
questions.explanation: The lecture advises, 'in your planning part of any planning you should always have a risk plan what things can go wrong may be a connectivity issue, maybe a server issue maybe a manpower issue the person suddenly leaves or whatever. So, all these risks need to be documented and the mitigation plan made.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'knowledge assessment criteria' in the transition process?
options: A) To determine employee salaries
B) To test if the person receiving knowledge has truly acquired it
C) To evaluate the performance of the trainers
D) To select new software tools
questions.answer: B) To test if the person receiving knowledge has truly acquired it
questions.explanation: The lecture asks, 'how will you test the knowledge level that whether we have reached that parallel part of the knowledge level how it has been reached, whether the person who is receiving the knowledge has really got the knowledge of not. So, there is an assessment criteria checklist.'

questions.question: Why are documents like the Application Information Document (AID) considered 'dynamic documents'?
options: A) They are stored in a cloud-based system
B) They are constantly updated to reflect changes in the system
C) They can be accessed from anywhere
D) They are only relevant for a short period
questions.answer: B) They are constantly updated to reflect changes in the system
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'These documents always get updated. These are all dynamic document because anytime you do a change, so that the document has to get now updated because a change has to be reflected in your documentation.'

questions.question: Why is it important to maintain a recording repository of knowledge transfer recordings?
options: A) To reduce paper usage
B) To provide training for new team members who join later
C) To prove that training was conducted
D) To comply with data retention policies
questions.answer: B) To provide training for new team members who join later
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'all this knowledge transfer recordings you have to keep in a repository because every time a new person joins in your team he has to go through all that and because every time a new person comes to your project he has to be trained because team’s members are not permanent.'

questions.question: What is a potential negative consequence if the transition project management is not done successfully due to inadequate knowledge?
options: A) Increased employee satisfaction
B) Contractual failures and financial penalties
C) Faster project completion
D) Reduced need for documentation
questions.answer: B) Contractual failures and financial penalties
questions.explanation: The lecture warns, 'if this there is a problem here, it does not it has been not done very successfully then you will have problems later on when you are actually delivering your service, there will be contractual failures. And, you will not be able to meet contractual requirements to do it in time because of inadequate knowledge; that means penalty, financial penalty.'

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Plan (DR/BCP) in the context of IT system support?
options: A) To reduce operational costs
B) To ensure continuous support even during unforeseen events like natural disasters or political problems
C) To train employees on new technologies
D) To manage daily system backups
questions.answer: B) To ensure continuous support even during unforeseen events like natural disasters or political problems
questions.explanation: The lecture discusses DR/BCP in scenarios like 'something happens in Bangalore, how will you support? Suppose there is a political problem people cannot go to the office or there is a natural disaster... How will you support that? What is your business continuity plan?'

questions.question: The lecture mentions transitioning as a part of MIS. What does MIS stand for in this context?
options: A) Management Information Systems
B) Manufacturing Integration Systems
C) Marketing Intelligence Solutions
D) Mobile Internet Services
questions.answer: A) Management Information Systems
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'It is part of MIS but its, I am saying within this section of managing global organizations, global project.' MIS commonly stands for Management Information Systems in academic contexts.

questions.question: Which countries are mentioned as examples of 'low cost centers' for offshoring IT services?
options: A) USA, UK, Germany
B) India, Philippines, Brazil
C) Japan, China, South Korea
D) Canada, Australia, New Zealand
questions.answer: B) India, Philippines, Brazil
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'All of these services delivery organizations which is developed in countries or like India, Philippines, Brazil, etcetera the low cost centers countries.'

questions.question: Besides client to new service provider, what other scenario for knowledge transition is mentioned?
options: A) From end-users to developers
B) From project team to support team within the same organization
C) From management to HR
D) From sales to marketing
questions.answer: B) From project team to support team within the same organization
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'this involves transferring the knowledge from the implementation team to support team or from client to new service provider... So, this is happening within the organization.'

questions.question: What specific communication challenge is highlighted when offshoring to India, even though English is widely spoken?
options: A) Lack of vocabulary
B) Different accents and communication styles
C) Inability to write in English
D) Preference for native languages
questions.answer: B) Different accents and communication styles
questions.explanation: The lecture notes, 'their style of speaking English is different, the accent is different... And in India not that everybody is good in English. Many our people have studied say in the vernacular medium schools... But their English communication skill both spoken and written may not be of certain standard.'

questions.question: Why is testing crucial when implementing changes in an IT system?
options: A) To speed up the deployment process
B) To ensure the changes do not disrupt existing programs
C) To reduce the cost of development
D) To document the changes for future reference
questions.answer: B) To ensure the changes do not disrupt existing programs
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Testing while implementing changes for any change there has to be a test of course, because any change should not distract disturb the existing programs.'

questions.question: In the context of IT environments (development, QA, production), what happens in the 'production environment'?
options: A) New code is written
B) Quality checks are performed
C) The actual system is used by end-users
D) Training is conducted
questions.answer: C) The actual system is used by end-users
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the production environment as 'where the actual thing happens... people will actually start using it.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'value realization' and 'measuring business benefit' as part of continuous improvement?
options: A) To justify the cost of IT staff
B) To demonstrate the tangible benefits and improvements achieved by IT initiatives
C) To determine employee bonuses
D) To compare with competitors
questions.answer: B) To demonstrate the tangible benefits and improvements achieved by IT initiatives
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'the company will ask what is the business benefit I am getting; so finally, you have to every year on year or quarter on quarter, you have to solve, find out some metrics which are measured; you have to tell them; so like this year it was this; so next year the value was this, so you have, you know done some so much improvement, etc. And we are measuring business benefits also.'

questions.question: What are the two major components of 'Application Development and Maintenance (ADM)'?
options: A) Planning and Testing
B) Development and Maintenance
C) Offshoring and Transitioning
D) Hardware and Software
questions.answer: B) Development and Maintenance
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states, 'So, basically we say application development and maintenance. So, the two major components, one is development, other is a maintenance.'

questions.question: What is the typical timeframe mentioned for a transition phase?
options: A) A few days
B) 2 months, 3 months, or 6-8 weeks
C) Several years
D) Indefinite
questions.answer: B) 2 months, 3 months, or 6-8 weeks
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'transition starts the phase; it could be a 2 months, 3 months sort of timeframe what we are talking about this transition what happens, takes place... it is a mini project you can say 3 weeks or 2 months, 6 weeks, 8 weeks.'

questions.question: What does RKT stand for in the context of the transition phases diagram?
options: A) Remote Key Technology
B) Rapid Knowledge Transfer
C) Remote Knowledge Transfer
D) Real-time Knowledge Tracking
questions.answer: C) Remote Knowledge Transfer
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'this RKT means you are using Remote Knowledge Transfer.'

questions.question: Which of the following is a deliverable of the 'transition master planning'?
options: A) End-user training modules
B) Master transition plan
C) Root cause analysis reports
D) Application enhancement requests
questions.answer: B) Master transition plan
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'the master transition plan' as a deliverable of the planning.

questions.question: What does 'in-flight projects' refer to in the context of application-specific planning deliverables?
options: A) Projects that have already been completed
B) Current existing software development projects that are not yet complete
C) Projects that are being flown to another country
D) Projects that are experiencing delays
questions.answer: B) Current existing software development projects that are not yet complete
questions.explanation: The lecture defines 'in flight projects, means the current existing software development projects which are going on in that organization, not yet complete, not yet implemented.'

questions.question: Why is 'key resource identification' important in transition planning, especially for disaster recovery?
options: A) To assign them to less critical tasks
B) To ensure they have necessary infrastructure (e.g., laptops, broadband) to work remotely during emergencies
C) To reduce their workload
D) To provide them with additional vacation time
questions.answer: B) To ensure they have necessary infrastructure (e.g., laptops, broadband) to work remotely during emergencies
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Key resource means you have to keep and remember, some of high resource are very key they are handling with the key functions. If something goes wrong they have to be immediately start working from home. So, they have to be given laptop right from beginning. We have to see that their broadband is working from home.'

questions.question: What type of tools are used for Remote Knowledge Transfer (RKT)?
options: A) Only physical documents
B) Collaboration tools like video conferencing and recording software
C) Only email communication
D) Traditional classroom settings
questions.answer: B) Collaboration tools like video conferencing and recording software
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Remote knowledge transfer tool is again a collaboration tool... recording training session, then replay, reuse, a collaboration and also you can do it as it during your steady state... like a today’s we are using Zoom video or Google Meet and things like that.'

questions.question: Why is it critical for the receiving team to clarify all doubts and ask all relevant questions during the fixed transition time?
options: A) To impress the trainers
B) Because the experts providing training might not be available for follow-up questions later
C) To extend the transition period
D) To reduce the amount of documentation needed
questions.answer: B) Because the experts providing training might not be available for follow-up questions later
questions.explanation: The lecture stresses, 'all doubts questions etcetera knowledge related should have to be clarified within this fixed time... If you miss out something after that, those experts are no longer there because they have lost their job, they have gone somewhere else and after, they leave the company, they will not bother if you contact them.'

questions.question: The lecture states that IT is a knowledge-based industry with 'no physical involvement.' Which of the following is given as an example of a physical involvement NOT present in IT?
options: A) Changing code
B) Researching software issues
C) Replacing a part or component like a motherboard
D) Studying software
questions.answer: C) Replacing a part or component like a motherboard
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts IT with physical work: 'it is not you know screwdriver or you maintaining something welding, cutting, breaking, etc... You are not you know replacing a part or replacing a component or replacing a chip or replacing a motherboard like the server etcetera; so, no hardware.'

questions.question: What is the typical resolution time for a Severity 2 ticket, as mentioned in the lecture?
options: A) 1-2 hours
B) 4-8 hours
C) 24 hours
D) Several days
questions.answer: B) 4-8 hours
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'If it is a severity 2 ticket... Then, it will probably give you some more time SLA will say you have to solve this problem in 4 hours or sometimes in 8 hours maximum, say 8 hours is just one day one working day.'

questions.question: When handling HR transition, why is it described as a 'changed management activity' that is not always easy?
options: A) Because HR personnel lack technical skills
B) Because people have many questions, doubts, and fears about changing companies and roles
C) Because it involves complex legal procedures
D) Because it requires extensive travel
questions.answer: B) Because people have many questions, doubts, and fears about changing companies and roles
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'when you are handling people changing people again it is not always easy job because they will have a lot of questions, they have lot of doubts, that have lot of fears and you have to all as a HR person you have to satisfy, that the satisfy their questions.'

questions.question: What type of knowledge is included in 'application-specific knowledge' during knowledge transfer?
options: A) General business processes
B) The logics for configuration and development
C) HR policies
D) Global market trends
questions.answer: B) The logics for configuration and development
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'then the application-specific; for each application; there will be application-specific knowledge and the logics for configuration development, etc.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT categorized as a typical maintenance service in an IT system, according to the lecture?
options: A) Service request
B) Emergency fix
C) Application enhancement
D) Corrective maintenance
questions.answer: C) Application enhancement
questions.explanation: The lecture categorizes 'service request type, ongoing maintenance, emergency fix, corrective maintenance, database services' as maintenance. It explicitly states 'application enhancement and data services is development.'

questions.question: According to the lecture, which period is characterized by 'brawn' and colonization by countries?
options: B) 2000 and beyond
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'globalization 1.0 is 1492 Columbus set sail to US. And that from 1492 to 1800 that is all the colonizations were taking place. How brawn, how much muscle, Colonization by countries...'

questions.question: The era of Globalization 2.0, from 1800 to 2000, is primarily defined by breakthroughs at which level?
options: A) Individual level
B) Country level
C) Company level
D) Regional level
questions.answer: C) Company level
questions.explanation: The lecture describes Globalization 2.0 as '1800 to 2000 where company level, breakthroughs in transportation and telecommunication costs...'

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of Globalization 3.0, which began in 2000 and continues to the present?
options: A) Colonization by countries
B) Company-level transportation breakthroughs
C) Individual-level connectivity, software, and collaboration
D) Centralized economic planning
questions.answer: C) Individual-level connectivity, software, and collaboration
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Then globalization 3.0 is at the individual level which is from 2000 and beyond to the present; its connectivity allowed connectivity software and collaboration.'

questions.question: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 is identified as a major flattening factor because it led to what?
options: A) The invention of the World Wide Web
B) The collapse of communism and the rise of free market societies
C) The widespread adoption of workflow software
D) The beginning of large-scale IT outsourcing
questions.answer: B) The collapse of communism and the rise of free market societies
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'flattener 1... Berlin Wall comes down. Tipping point for free market societies... communism was almost practically not there – dead.'

questions.question: The Netscape IPO in 1995 is cited as a flattening factor primarily due to its role in:
options: A) Establishing the first social media platform
B) Making the World Wide Web universally accessible and usable
C) Introducing the concept of cloud computing
D) Developing advanced graphics for video games
questions.answer: B) Making the World Wide Web universally accessible and usable
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Netscape the famous browser... opened up a world for us, because now we could browse through our computer and get lot of information... Universal usability, accessibility and interoperability of the Web...'

questions.question: How did workflow software contribute to the flattening of the world?
options: A) By enabling individuals to create personal websites
B) By allowing applications to communicate and facilitating collaboration
C) By reducing the cost of physical transportation
D) By standardizing global currency exchange rates
questions.answer: B) By allowing applications to communicate and facilitating collaboration
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Flattener 3, the workflow software. Have your applications talk to my application. How the applications talk to each other? Collaboration, rapid deployment, rapid development...'

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the 'uploading' flattening factor, as described in the lecture?
options: A) The development of steam engines
B) The creation of multinational corporations
C) The open source movement, including projects like Wikipedia and Linux
D) The establishment of global supply chains
questions.answer: C) The open source movement, including projects like Wikipedia and Linux
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Uploading open source movement that is where something which started open source movement. Self-organizing collaborative communities; like the Linux Operating System or the Firefox browser or the Wikipedia for example.'

questions.question: The lecture identifies the Y2K problem in 1999 as a significant catalyst for the growth of which flattening factor, particularly for India?
options: A) Offshoring
B) Insourcing
C) Outsourcing
D) Supply-chaining
questions.answer: C) Outsourcing
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states, 'Outsourcing, yes of course, we are very familiar with that Y2K, it started with Y2K in 1999, 98, 99. An Indian major outsourcing started with this.'

questions.question: What is the primary economic imperative for companies to engage in outsourcing, as discussed in the lecture?
options: A) To increase brand recognition globally
B) To save costs by accessing skilled resources at a lower price
C) To gain control over foreign markets
D) To reduce transportation expenses
questions.answer: B) To save costs by accessing skilled resources at a lower price
questions.explanation: The lecture explains outsourcing as 'competent programmers and engineers who will deliver same quality at a lower cost, cost arbitrage... economic imperative, cost saving getting large volume of skilled resource...'

questions.question: How does offshoring differ from outsourcing, according to the lecture?
options: A) Offshoring involves keeping operations within the same country.
B) Offshoring specifically refers to sending operations to another country.
C) Offshoring is limited to manufacturing, while outsourcing includes services.
D) Offshoring focuses on core activities, while outsourcing handles non-core.
questions.answer: B) Offshoring specifically refers to sending operations to another country.
questions.explanation: The lecture defines offshoring as 'just an extension outsourcing. See instead of just outsourcing, I mean to say third party I am send it out to another country that is where all the cost and all these advantage will come.'

questions.question: Beyond manufacturing, which of the following services were also subject to offshoring, as mentioned in the lecture?
options: A) Only core business strategy development
B) Legal processing, medical transcription, and accounting back office
C) Local retail sales and distribution
D) Raw material extraction
questions.answer: B) Legal processing, medical transcription, and accounting back office
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'It not just manufacturing but also and not limited to, outsourcing was not only to manufacturing, but legal processing, medical transcription, consulting service, accounting back office.'

questions.question: The lecture uses the example of Levi's denim cloth coming from Arvind Mills in India and garments from Bangladesh to illustrate which flattening factor?
options: A) Offshoring
B) Insourcing
C) Supply-chaining
D) In-forming
questions.answer: C) Supply-chaining
questions.explanation: The lecture discusses, 'Supply-chaining, the whole apparel industry for example... the entire Levi’s material for the denim jeans the denim cloth comes from Arvind Mills supplied mostly by Arvind Mills of India. Bangladesh is supplying the entire readymade garments...'

questions.question: What technology is specifically mentioned as being used by Wal-Mart to manage its supply chain and track inventory?
options: A) Global Positioning System (GPS)
B) Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)
C) Near Field Communication (NFC)
D) Barcode scanners only
questions.answer: B) Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'RFID, Radio Frequency Identification, these are the tools or technologies which are used in order to manage the whole thing much faster way... Where RFIDs can be used to track your inventory, how it is moving.'

questions.question: The example of UPS fixing Toshiba laptops and delivering Papa John's Pizza supplies is used to illustrate which flattening factor?
options: A) Outsourcing
B) Offshoring
C) Insourcing
D) Supply-chaining
questions.answer: C) Insourcing
questions.explanation: The lecture describes, 'Insourcing. UPS one of the largest courier service company has an intimate collaboration relationship... An example is flexing fixing a Toshiba laptop... So, this is not a something called insourcing.'

questions.question: What does the lecture suggest 'insourcing' can involve for an organization like Swiggy?
options: A) Reducing their service offerings to focus on a single core activity.
B) Expanding their service offerings to include new types of deliveries, like groceries.
C) Moving their entire operations to a different country.
D) Selling off non-core business units.
questions.answer: B) Expanding their service offerings to include new types of deliveries, like groceries.
questions.explanation: The lecture uses Swiggy as an example: 'Swiggy... started delivering grocery as well. So, they just extending, that is called insourcing...'

questions.question: Which company is highlighted as a prime example of the 'in-forming' flattening factor, with its search engine becoming a verb?
options: A) Netscape
B) Microsoft
C) Google
D) Apple
questions.answer: C) Google
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'In-forming... Google, it is just the example now 1 billion searches per day... So, Google has become a verb; it is not only a noun, but it is also used to be the verb, so Google it means, do it, Google it – search for it...'

questions.question: The lecture mentions Wikipedia as an example of 'in-forming' due to its role in:
options: A) Centralized information control
B) Knowledge sharing and crowd-sourced content
C) Proprietary software development
D) Physical product distribution
questions.answer: B) Knowledge sharing and crowd-sourced content
questions.explanation: The lecture links Wikipedia to 'in-forming' and 'knowledge sharing,' describing it as a 'free encyclopedia and it is been continuously developed. It is a crowd sourced, or crowd developed information system.'

questions.question: According to Carly Fiorina, what key transformation helped flatten the world, acting as 'steroids'?
options: A) Making manufacturing processes more efficient
B) Making collaboration digital, mobile, personal, and virtual
C) Reducing international trade tariffs
D) Developing new forms of physical transportation
questions.answer: B) Making collaboration digital, mobile, personal, and virtual
questions.explanation: The lecture quotes Carly Fiorina: 'making collaboration digital, mobile, personal, virtual, this statement is made by Carly Fiorina... making collaboration digital. So, when we made collaboration into digital, mobile, personal, virtual, then it really the world became flat.'

questions.question: Which aspect of computing capabilities is listed as a 'steroid' that enabled the flattening of the world?
options: A) Decreased processing speed
B) Increased cost of storage
C) Enhanced speed, input/output rate, and storage capacity
D) Limited access to computing devices
questions.answer: C) Enhanced speed, input/output rate, and storage capacity
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Computing capabilities, including speed, input output rate, and storage capacity' as steroids.

questions.question: What communication technologies are mentioned as 'steroids' that helped flatten the world by enabling fast, free, and global communication?
options: A) Telegraph and telephone
B) Instant messaging, file sharing (e.g., BitTorrent), and VoIP (e.g., Skype)
C) Postal service and fax machines
D) Radio and television broadcasts
questions.answer: B) Instant messaging, file sharing (e.g., BitTorrent), and VoIP (e.g., Skype)
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions 'Instant messaging and file sharing – BitTorrent, Kazaa or whatever' and 'VoIP same thing Skype and nowadays, all these Zooms and Google Meet and all that these thing...' as steroids.

questions.question: The lecture emphasizes that information technology and information systems are essential for globalization because:
options: A) They are primarily used for entertainment.
B) Without them, globalization would not have been possible or achieved its 'flatness.'
C) They only facilitate communication within a single country.
D) They are solely responsible for physical product manufacturing.
questions.answer: B) Without them, globalization would not have been possible or achieved its 'flatness.'
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'you can see how information technology, information system is an essential ingredient of globalization. Without this, globalization would not have been possible, you could have it have made it flat flatness...'

questions.question: The concept of 'Globalization of Corporates in a Flat World' is heavily influenced by which author and his book?
options: A) Bill Gates, 'The Road Ahead'
B) Thomas Friedman, 'The World is Flat'
C) Peter Drucker, 'Management'
D) Michael Porter, 'Competitive Strategy'
questions.answer: B) Thomas Friedman, 'The World is Flat'
questions.explanation: The lecture begins by stating, 'So, it started with this flat world, there is a famous book: ‘The World is Flat’ by Thomas Friedman...'

questions.question: The collapse of communism, triggered by the fall of the Berlin Wall, led to a shift away from what economic model?
options: A) Free market economies
B) Capitalist systems
C) Central planning economies
D) Mixed economies
questions.answer: C) Central planning economies
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Moved away from central planning, because communism again these are you know the central planning economies like China for example...'

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web, four years before the Netscape IPO in 1995?
options: A) Steve Jobs
B) Bill Gates
C) Tim Berners-Lee
D) Mark Zuckerberg
questions.answer: C) Tim Berners-Lee
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, '1995 Netscape IPO 4 years after Berners-Lee Tim Berners-Lee invented the Web: ‘www’.'

questions.question: The 'Win 95 shift' refers to the introduction of what, which changed how personal computers were used?
options: A) Command-line interface
B) Graphic User Interface (GUI)
C) Text-based operating system
D) Punch card system
questions.answer: B) Graphic User Interface (GUI)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Win 95 shift; it is Windows 95 – the graphic user interface; very famous; Guvi. So, that is also it was gradually changing the way you we use PCs...'

questions.question: Workflow software facilitates 'cheapest sources for coding, test, implementation' by enabling what?
options: A) Physical relocation of entire development teams
B) Collaboration and rapid deployment across geographical boundaries
C) Exclusive use of proprietary software
D) Manual data entry and processing
questions.answer: B) Collaboration and rapid deployment across geographical boundaries
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Flattener 3, the workflow software... Collaboration, rapid deployment, rapid development, cheapest sources for coding, test, implementation...'

questions.question: Besides Linux and Firefox, which other platform is mentioned as an example of the open source movement and crowd-sourced information?
options: A) Encyclopedia Britannica
B) Microsoft Word
C) Wikipedia
D) Google Search
questions.answer: C) Wikipedia
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'like the Linux Operating System or the Firefox browser or the Wikipedia for example' as examples of the open source movement.

questions.question: What was the core issue of the Y2K problem that led to a surge in outsourcing to India?
options: A) A shortage of computer hardware globally.
B) The inability of computers to process dates beyond 1999 due to two-digit year fields.
C) A virus that corrupted all computer systems in 1999.
D) A lack of internet connectivity for global collaboration.
questions.answer: B) The inability of computers to process dates beyond 1999 due to two-digit year fields.
questions.explanation: The lecture details, 'There was because the previous thing it was all and the date for field was had to be changed; because the year was two digits; so, 99 so 98, 99 not 1999. So, if it is 98 and 99, and then suddenly the after 99, we will have 00. So, how will be the computers resistance react?'

questions.question: The lecture uses Apple's focus on designing iPhones, rather than manufacturing them, to illustrate the principle of:
options: A) Vertical integration
B) Outsourcing non-core activities to focus on core competencies
C) Insourcing all production processes
D) Centralized planning
questions.answer: B) Outsourcing non-core activities to focus on core competencies
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, the idea was developing gradually try to outsource all your non-core activity, so that you focus really on your core activities. Let us say for example, Apple, core activity is designing iPhone, not manufacturing...'

questions.question: What term is used in the lecture to describe the outsourcing of legal processing?
options: A) BPO (Business Process Outsourcing)
B) KPO (Knowledge Process Outsourcing)
C) LPO (Legal Process Outsourcing)
D) IPO (Initial Public Offering)
questions.answer: C) LPO (Legal Process Outsourcing)
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Legal processing is been done in a big way KPO knowledge it is LPO, it is called LPO, Legal Process Outsourcing.'

questions.question: For a large organization like Wal-Mart, what is considered a key competitive advantage in managing its supply chain?
options: A) Manual inventory tracking
B) Limited supplier relationships
C) Robust IT infrastructure
D) Exclusive reliance on local suppliers
questions.answer: C) Robust IT infrastructure
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Supply chain; Wal-Mart... IT infrastructure is a key competitive advantage.'

questions.question: How is RFID technology used in the business environment, according to the lecture?
options: A) To process credit card payments at checkout.
B) To track inventory movement and status automatically.
C) To provide wireless internet access.
D) To encrypt sensitive data during transmission.
questions.answer: B) To track inventory movement and status automatically.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Where RFIDs can be used to track your inventory, how it is moving. So, when it moves and it gets distract, it is generating information.'

questions.question: When UPS delivers Papa John's Pizza supplies or packages tropical fish, it is an example of insourcing because:
options: A) UPS is outsourcing these tasks to other companies.
B) UPS is expanding its traditional courier services into value-added logistics.
C) Papa John's and Segrest Farms are taking these activities in-house.
D) It represents a return to core business activities for UPS.
questions.answer: B) UPS is expanding its traditional courier services into value-added logistics.
questions.explanation: The lecture describes UPS's activities as 'extending into various types of activities to increase their revenue of course, and that is it is a change in their business model.' This aligns with the insourcing concept of diversifying services.

questions.question: The lecture highlights Google's impact on 'in-forming' by noting that:
options: A) It was the first company to offer email services.
B) Its name has become a verb, signifying searching for information.
C) It developed the first web browser.
D) It is primarily a hardware manufacturer.
questions.answer: B) Its name has become a verb, signifying searching for information.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, Google has become a verb; it is not only a noun, but it is also used to be the verb, so Google it means, do it, Google it – search for it...'

questions.question: The 'steroids' flattening factor includes the observation that communication costs are:
options: A) Steadily increasing, limiting global interaction.
B) Coming down, encouraging more widespread use of technology.
C) Remaining stable, with no significant impact.
D) Only decreasing for large corporations.
questions.answer: B) Coming down, encouraging more widespread use of technology.
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Communication costs are coming down, so all communication cost, the internet cost, the bandwidth costs are coming down. So, obviously, when this cost come down, it encourages technology.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the three powerful technological forces contributing to the 'great convergence' that flattened the world?
options: A) Low-cost and powerful computing devices
B) High-cost, low-bandwidth network connectivity
C) Low-cost, high-bandwidth network connectivity
D) Open standards
questions.answer: B) High-cost, low-bandwidth network connectivity
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Low cost and powerful computing device; low-cost, high bandwidth network connectivity; open standards' as the three forces. Option B contradicts the second point.

questions.question: The BRIC countries (Brazil, Russia, India, China) are mentioned in the lecture as examples of:
options: A) Developed nations that are part of the G7 group.
B) Emerging regions whose economic situations are influenced by globalization.
C) Countries that resist globalization and central planning.
D) Nations primarily focused on insourcing activities.
questions.answer: B) Emerging regions whose economic situations are influenced by globalization.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, the emerging region like a BRIC countries for example... again part of the flattening. So, they are relate, clubbed together.'

questions.question: Which historical event marks the beginning of Globalization 1.0, according to the lecture?
options: A) The invention of the steam engine
B) Columbus setting sail to the US in 1492
C) The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989
D) The Netscape IPO in 1995
questions.answer: B) Columbus setting sail to the US in 1492
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'globalization 1.0 is 1492 Columbus set sail to US.'

questions.question: Which of these technologies was NOT a key breakthrough during Globalization 2.0 (1800-2000)?
options: A) Steam engines
B) Telegraphs
C) Fiber optics
D) Advanced video conferencing (e.g., Zoom)
questions.answer: D) Advanced video conferencing (e.g., Zoom)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'railway, ships, steam engines, telegraphs, telephone, PC – computer, fiber optics, internet' for G2.0. Advanced video conferencing like Zoom is associated with G3.0 and 'steroids.'

questions.question: Why is MIS (Management Information Systems) particularly relevant to Globalization 3.0?
options: A) It focuses on physical infrastructure development.
B) It is directly related to connectivity, software, and collaboration.
C) It primarily deals with colonial administration.
D) It is concerned with brawn and muscle power.
questions.answer: B) It is directly related to connectivity, software, and collaboration.
questions.explanation: The lecture asks, 'why MIS is getting into it here is because of connectivity, software and collaboration. The whole subject is our information technology related.'

questions.question: The lecture refers to the 'Iron Curtain' in the context of the Berlin Wall's fall, implying that before 1989, these countries were:
options: A) Highly transparent and open to the world.
B) Basically invisible and not transparent to outsiders.
C) Leaders in global trade and commerce.
D) Primarily focused on capitalist expansion.
questions.answer: B) Basically invisible and not transparent to outsiders.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'It was the Iron Curtain, we say countries basically there were nothing were visible they were not transparent, we were not aware what was happening there, but now things opened up.'

questions.question: The universal usability and accessibility of the Web, facilitated by browsers, meant that:
options: A) Users needed specific software for each document format.
B) Documents could only be viewed in a proprietary format.
C) Browsers became software and technology independent, allowing access to various document formats.
D) Only text-based information was accessible.
questions.answer: C) Browsers became software and technology independent, allowing access to various document formats.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'The browser became software independent, technology independent. See your document or information can be in any format, PDF Acrobat, Word - MS Word, whatever Excel, if you have a browser you can access these documents technology agnostic.'

questions.question: India became a major hub for outsourcing due to its ability to provide:
options: A) Cheap raw materials for manufacturing.
B) A large volume of skilled programmers and engineers at a lower cost.
C) Exclusive access to advanced proprietary technology.
D) A large consumer market for outsourced products.
questions.answer: B) A large volume of skilled programmers and engineers at a lower cost.
questions.explanation: The lecture highlights, 'competent programmers and engineers who will deliver same quality at a lower cost, cost arbitrage... getting large volume of skilled resource... almost produce almost 1 million or 10 lakh engineers every year.'

questions.question: The lecture mentions that extensive offshoring of manufacturing led to what problem for countries like the US?
options: A) An increase in domestic manufacturing jobs.
B) A trade surplus with other nations.
C) A problem of trade deficit and the disappearance of domestic factories.
D) A decrease in global competition.
questions.answer: C) A problem of trade deficit and the disappearance of domestic factories.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'entire manufacturing virtually disappeared from US, all the steel plants closed down, most of the automobile factories closed down... there is a it was a problem which is happening now. So, there is lot of trade deficit.'

questions.question: UPS's expansion into services like managing Papa John's supplies or packaging fish is driven by what primary motivation?
options: A) To reduce their own operational costs.
B) To increase their revenue by diversifying their business model.
C) To acquire new manufacturing capabilities.
D) To compete directly with traditional retail stores.
questions.answer: B) To increase their revenue by diversifying their business model.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'they are extending into various types of activities to increase their revenue of course, and that is it is a change in their business model.'

questions.question: How did instant messaging and file sharing contribute to the flattening of the world?
options: A) By creating new physical barriers between countries.
B) By making communication more expensive.
C) By allowing seamless, fast, and practically free sharing of information across geographical boundaries.
D) By limiting access to information to specific regions.
questions.answer: C) By allowing seamless, fast, and practically free sharing of information across geographical boundaries.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Instant messaging and file sharing... helped communication... share anything across the world very fast... there is nowhere a restriction geographical restriction, so that is the geographic bar has completely collapsed.'

questions.question: What is the distinguishing feature of 'telepresence' as described in the lecture, particularly popularized by Cisco?
options: A) It is a low-quality audio-only communication system.
B) It provides high-quality video conferencing that makes participants feel physically together.
C) It is a system for remote control of physical robots.
D) It is a method for secure data encryption.
questions.answer: B) It provides high-quality video conferencing that makes participants feel physically together.
questions.explanation: The lecture describes 'Telepresence of high quality video conferencing where you literally feel as if the you are together in the same place that is why they gave the name telepresence.'

questions.question: The 'open standards' aspect of the great convergence implies that:
options: A) Most software and apps require significant payment.
B) Users are forced to buy proprietary systems.
C) Many software, technologies, and apps are free or easily accessible without proprietary restrictions.
D) Only government agencies can access certain technologies.
questions.answer: C) Many software, technologies, and apps are free or easily accessible without proprietary restrictions.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'open standards... I do not have to buy anything. So, these are all free, many software’s, many technologies, many apps, all the apps we get most of them are free. So, we can use it; you do not have to pay for it.'

questions.question: How did the COVID-19 pandemic serve as an example of the 'flattening' of the world, according to the lecture?
options: A) It led to increased national isolation and reduced global travel.
B) It demonstrated how information (e.g., mask use, social distancing) flowed seamlessly and instantaneously globally.
C) It highlighted the dominance of local economies over global ones.
D) It showed a decrease in the use of digital communication tools.
questions.answer: B) It demonstrated how information (e.g., mask use, social distancing) flowed seamlessly and instantaneously globally.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'COVID-19... how this is been its completely global. So, everybody in the world, we are talking about the same thing everywhere... The information is flowing seamlessly across instantaneously.'

questions.question: The ultimate outcome of the flattening of the world, as summarized in the lecture, is that individuals can now:
options: A) Only access information from their local communities.
B) Compute everywhere and anywhere, anytime, with access to limitless information and services.
C) Rely solely on physical mail for communication.
D) Only conduct business within their national borders.
questions.answer: B) Compute everywhere and anywhere, anytime, with access to limitless information and services.
questions.explanation: The lecture summarizes, 'So, let us summarize we are computing everywhere and anywhere, anytime and all the time with access to limitless amount of information and services.'
